Bay of Bengal Precipitation Forecast Revision App: Full Project Plan
Prepared for Durga Venkata Prasad Rapeti, QUEST Lab pre-doctoral Project 1. Date: 15 Nov 2026. One document holding the PRD, data design, architecture, agent design, UI wireframes, test plan, deployment plan and ready-to-paste Antigravity prompts.
0. Read this first
Verified so far (Step 1, from ECMWF pages, 15 Nov 2026): IFS stream class=od, stream=oper, type=fc; AIFS Single model=aifs-single, class=ai, stream=oper, type=fc; precipitation parameter tp (IFS paramId 228, AIFS paramId 228228); tp is accumulated from the start of the forecast; licence CC BY 4.0 plus ECMWF Terms of Use with required attribution wording; AIFS is 0.25° only, 6-hourly to 360 h.
Not verified (must be closed before coding the parser):
• Units from a real file. Documentation suggests IFS tp is metres and AIFS tp is kg m⁻² (equal to mm). Never assume; the parser reads the GRIB units key and converts.
• A real downloaded GRIB file. My sandbox could not reach ECMWF. Run the Phase 1 script on your machine.
• Retention. ECMWF pages disagree (12 runs, about 2–3 days, versus about 4 days). Mirrors keep more, length not stated.
• IFS 06/18 UTC step range: 0–144 h on one page, 0–90 h on another.
• The exact AIFS file path (inferred from the official client code, not seen on a real file).
• Whether a plain public download needs an ECMWF service agreement. Ask ECMWF support.
• Antigravity details below come from third-party guides, not Google's own docs. Check them in the app.
Treat every item above as an open question, not a fact. Record answers in DECISIONS.md.
1. Product requirements (PRD)
Name (working): MonsoonDelta. One line: Shows the latest ECMWF precipitation forecast for the Bay of Bengal region (default Visakhapatnam), how much it has changed across recent model runs for the same valid time, and where IFS and AIFS disagree, in plain language, never as an official warning.
Users: a curious member of the public, a student, or an analyst in coastal Andhra Pradesh who wants to know whether a forecast is stable or shifting.
Core features (MVP, nothing more):
1.  Latest forecast: 6-hour precipitation totals (mm) for the next 5 days at a chosen location, for IFS and AIFS.
2.  Forecast revision: for one valid window, the value from each of the last N runs, plus latest-minus-previous change and the range across runs.
3.  Model disagreement: IFS minus AIFS for the same window, shown as a number and a map.
4.  Plain-language explanation generated from templates (not free-form AI text) so wording is deterministic and testable.
5.  Permanent disclaimer and attribution on every page.
Not in MVP: accounts, push alerts, ensemble probabilities, 0.1° data, other regions, user-uploaded data, any word like "warning", "alert" or "danger".
Required wording (draft, final text is your decision):
• Disclaimer: "This is automated model output from ECMWF IFS and AIFS. It is not an official forecast or warning. For official warnings, follow your national meteorological service (IMD in India) and local authorities."
• Attribution: "This service is based on data and products of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). © 2026 ECMWF. Source: www.ecmwf.int. CC BY 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. ECMWF does not accept any liability for any error or omission in the data, their availability, or for any loss or damage arising from their use. Values shown are derived (6-hour totals, differences between runs), so the material has been modified."
Success criteria: (a) numbers match a hand-checked toy example; (b) app loads under 3 s on a mobile connection for a cached region; (c) every page shows disclaimer and attribution; (d) a stale-data banner appears when the newest run is older than a set threshold; (e) public URL working.
2. Data design
2.1 What we fetch
For each run (date and cycle 00/06/12/18 UTC), for each model, parameter tp only, region subset (proposed box 5–23°N, 78–100°E; your decision), 0.25° grid.
IFS fc steps: 3-hourly early, 6-hourly later; AIFS 6-hourly. Common grid for comparison: 6-hour windows ending 00/06/12/18 UTC. Use only steps that are multiples of 6 so both models line up.
2.2 Accumulation maths (to be unit-tested by hand)
tp(step) is total since the run start. Window total for the 6 hours ending at step s: W(s) = tp(s) - tp(s-6), converted to mm. For s = 6, W(6) = tp(6) since tp(0) = 0.
Hand example (units): IFS, steps 12 and 18 read 0.002 m and 0.005 m. Difference 0.003 m = 3.0 mm. AIFS, the same steps read 2.0 and 5.0 kg m⁻². Difference 3.0 kg m⁻² = 3.0 mm. (1 kg m⁻² of water equals 1 mm depth.)
Guard rules: if a difference is below zero by more than a small tolerance (set after inspecting a real file), fail loudly; tiny negatives from packing may be clamped to 0 and logged. If the units key is not one of the two known values, stop and raise an error.
2.3 Revision calculation (to be unit-tested by hand)
Fix a valid window V (6 hours ending at time T). Each run r that covers V gives a value A_r(V). Take the last N runs (default 6), ordered oldest to newest.
• Latest change = A_latest - A_previous (mm).
• Range = max(A_r) - min(A_r) (mm).
• Direction = up, down or steady if |latest change| is below a tolerance (proposed 0.5 mm; your decision).
Hand example: runs 00Z, 06Z, 12Z give 4.0, 10.0, 7.0 mm for the same window. Latest change = 7.0 - 10.0 = -3.0 mm (down). Range = 10.0 - 4.0 = 6.0 mm. Only runs whose lead time covers V count; a run that does not cover V is skipped, never filled with zero.
2.4 Disagreement
For the same window and the same latest-run time as far as possible: D = IFS - AIFS (mm). Report absolute difference, and say which model is wetter. Do not report relative percent when both values are under 1 mm (avoids misleading ratios).
2.5 Location logic
Point view for Visakhapatnam: area mean of grid cells within a small radius or the 4 surrounding cells (your decision), not a single nearest cell. Approximate coordinates about 17.7°N, 83.2°E; verify before hard-coding. Region view: map of the latest 6-hour total and of D.
2.6 Descriptive bands (own, neutral)
Own bands for 6-hour totals, for example: under 1 mm, 1 to under 5, 5 to under 15, 15 to under 30, 30 and over. These are descriptive, not official categories. Do not reuse IMD rainfall class names unless you verify them and cite the source.
2.7 History
ECMWF keeps only a short window, so "last several runs" must come from either a mirror or our own stored history. Proposal: a scheduled job stores the region subset per run as small compressed files, retention 14 days. Needs your decision (see section 11).
3. System architecture
 ECMWF open data (data.ecmwf.int or cloud mirror)
        |  HTTPS, no key
        v
 [Ingest job, scheduled]  --fetch tp, IFS + AIFS, new runs only
   - check index/latest run, skip if already stored
   - read GRIB (cfgrib/eccodes), check units, subset region
   - write run file: store/{model}/{yyyymmddHH}/tp.nc (or .parquet)
        |
        v
 [Storage]  object store or disk volume, 14-day retention + manifest.json
        |
        v
 [Compute layer: pure Python library]
   accumulate(), to_mm(), window_totals(), revision(), disagreement(), explain()
        |
        v
 [API: FastAPI]  /api/latest  /api/revision  /api/disagreement  /api/health
        |   JSON + short cache (5 min), rate limit
        v
 [Web UI: static page or small React app + map]  disclaimer + attribution on every view
Principles: compute library has no web or file code, so tests run offline; ingest never runs inside a web request; API only reads precomputed or small cached data; one source of truth for units and constants.
Suggested stack (your decision): Python 3.12, ecmwf-opendata (client), cfgrib or eccodes, xarray, numpy, FastAPI, pytest, a static frontend (plain HTML/JS with Leaflet or a small chart library). Keep dependencies few.
4. Agent design (how Antigravity agents divide the work)
Four roles. Each is a separate conversation with its own scope, so changes stay reviewable.
Agent
Owns
Must not touch
Data agent
ingest, GRIB reading, units, subsetting, sample fixture
UI, API
Compute agent
accumulation, revision, disagreement, explanation templates, all tests
network code
API agent
FastAPI routes, caching, rate limit, health, stale banner data
compute maths
UI agent
pages, charts, map, copy, disclaimer, accessibility
data parsing
A fifth human role is you: you approve every plan, run the tests, read each diff, and write DECISIONS.md. Rule for every agent: read AGENTS.md first; never invent a number or source; ask before a design choice; commit small.
5. UI design (wireframes)
5.1 Dashboard (desktop)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| MonsoonDelta   Location: [Visakhapatnam v]   Window: [Next 5 days v]  [Info]   |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ! Automated model output, not an official forecast or warning.  [Details]      |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| LATEST 6-HOUR RAIN (mm)  IFS run: 12Z 15 Nov     AIFS run: 12Z 15 Nov          |
| bar chart: windows on x-axis, two bars per window (IFS, AIFS)                  |
+-----------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
| FORECAST REVISION  (window: [Tue 06-12])| MODEL DISAGREEMENT                   |
| line chart: last 6 runs -> mm           | map: IFS minus AIFS (diverging scale)|
| Latest change: -3.0 mm (down)           | Point: IFS 7.0, AIFS 3.0 mm          |
| Range across runs: 6.0 mm               | IFS wetter by 4.0 mm                 |
+-----------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
| IN PLAIN WORDS                                                               |
| "The newest run expects less rain than the one before for this period. The     |
|  two models differ by 4 mm. Treat this as one possible outcome."              |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Data freshness: updated 3 h ago | Attribution + licence line | Methods link     |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
5.2 Mobile
Single column in this order: disclaimer bar, location picker, latest chart, plain-words card, revision card, disagreement card (map collapsed), footer. Tap a chart bar to set the window.
5.3 Other screens
• Methods page: what a model run is, what "6-hour total" means, how revision and disagreement are computed, limits (coarse 0.25° grid, no local effects, model error), data source and licence.
• Stale/error state: "Latest data is older than expected. Showing the last available run from [time]."
• Empty state: when fewer than 2 runs cover the window, hide revision and say why.
5.4 Design rules
Colour-blind safe palette; never colour alone to carry meaning; units on every number; no red/alarm styling and no warning icons; text min 16 px; keyboard accessible; works at 360 px width.
6. Plain-language engine
Template-based and tested. Each sentence is chosen from a fixed set by rules on numbers (direction, size band, agreement). Example rules: direction up/down/steady; size small/moderate/large by band; agreement close if |D| under 2 mm else differ. Every output ends with the disclaimer link. Banned words list tested in CI: warning, alert, danger, evacuate, will flood, safe.
7. Test plan (offline, small saved sample)
1.  Fixture: one small GRIB or NetCDF per model, cropped to a few grid cells and 3 steps, saved in tests/data/ (a few KB). Never fetch in tests.
2.  Units test: IFS fixture in metres converts to mm; AIFS in kg m⁻² converts to mm; unknown units raise.
3.  Accumulation test: the 12 → 18 h example gives exactly 3.0 mm for both models; step 6 case; negative-difference guard.
4.  Revision test: the 4.0 / 10.0 / 7.0 example gives -3.0 change and 6.0 range; run that does not cover the window is skipped.
5.  Disagreement test: 7.0 vs 3.0 gives +4.0, IFS wetter; both under 1 mm gives no percent.
6.  Explanation test: fixed inputs give fixed sentences; banned words never appear.
7.  API tests: schema, stale flag, cache header, rate-limit response.
8.  Smoke test post-deploy: health endpoint and one real fetch, run manually or by a scheduled check, not in CI.
Commit rule: tests first for each calculation, then code, one commit each.
8. Deployment plan
• Repo: GitHub, MIT or similar licence for your code (ECMWF data licence is separate; keep attribution).
• CI: GitHub Actions running pytest and lint on each push.
• Hosting (your decision): one small container on a free or cheap host, with a persistent disk or object storage for the 14-day store; static frontend served by the same app or a static host.
• Scheduler: cron or scheduled job every 3 hours; checks if a new run exists; idempotent so re-runs do nothing.
• Config: environment variables for region box, retention, source name (ecmwf, aws, google); no secrets exist since no key is needed.
• Monitoring: /api/health returns newest run time per model; an uptime check pings it; stale banner if over threshold.
• Rollback: tag each release; keep previous container image.
9. What breaks first with 100 users at once (design answer, not your interview answer)
The likely first failure is anything that reads or processes GRIB on request. Mitigation built into the plan: ingest is offline and scheduled, the API serves small precomputed JSON, responses are cached for minutes, and the host's CPU and memory limits are the next ceiling. Second risk: the source rate limit if every user triggered a fetch, which this design avoids. Test it: run a simple load script against the deployed API and record the numbers; do not claim a capacity figure without a measurement.
10. Timeline (assumes about 4 working days; adjust)
• Day 0: Phase 1 file inspection on your machine, answer open items, set DECISIONS.md.
• Day 1: Phase 2 compute library and tests (units, accumulation, revision, disagreement).
• Day 2: Phase 3 ingest and storage; Phase 4 API.
• Day 3: Phase 5 UI and Methods page; plain-language engine.
• Day 4: Phase 6 deploy, scheduler, load check; Phase 7 README, final review.
11. Decisions you must make
1.  How to get history: use a cloud mirror, ECMWF only (about 8–12 runs), or store our own (recommended, adds a job).
2.  Region box and default point method (4-cell mean vs radius mean).
3.  Window size: 6 hours for both models (proposed).
4.  Revision tolerance (0.5 mm proposed) and descriptive bands.
5.  Hosting provider and storage type.
6.  Frontend: plain HTML/JS (simpler, proposed) or React.
7.  Whether to ask ECMWF about the service agreement before going public.
12. Antigravity workflow
Facts from third-party guides (verify in the app): Antigravity is Google's agent-first IDE, launched Nov 2025, with an Agent Manager, Planning mode (plan first) and Fast mode, artifacts such as plans, task lists and walkthroughs, and rules and workflows. Version 2.0 (May 2026) moved toward a separate app, and the guides say the IDE's Agent Manager may be removed later. One guide says workspace rules live in .agent/rules/ and workflows in .agent/workflows/; another says .antigravity/. Open Customizations in the app and use whichever path it shows.
How to run it: use Planning mode for every phase; read the plan before approving; set permissions to ask before running terminal commands and before network calls; one agent per phase; end each phase with tests passing, a git commit, and a DECISIONS.md line.
12.1 AGENTS.md / rules file (paste as workspace rule)
Project: MonsoonDelta, ECMWF IFS/AIFS precipitation revision app (Bay of Bengal, default Visakhapatnam).
Rules:
1. Never invent numbers, sources, file paths or API fields. If unverified, write UNVERIFIED and ask me.
2. Never read, print or write secrets. No keys are needed. Do not add any.
3. Small steps. State plan and assumptions first. Wait for my decision on any real choice.
4. Commit often with clear messages (imperative, one change each). Tests before code.
5. Tests run offline on tests/data fixtures. Never download in tests.
6. Units: always read the GRIB units key; convert to mm; unknown units raise an error.
7. tp is accumulated from forecast start; window total = tp(s) - tp(s-6).
8. UI and copy never say warning/alert/danger; every page shows the disclaimer and ECMWF attribution.
9. Keep dependencies minimal. Python 3.12, pytest, FastAPI.
10. Update DECISIONS.md after every decision (what, why, date).
12.2 Workflow prompts (save as slash workflows)
/plan-phase
Read AGENTS.md and DECISIONS.md. For the phase I name, produce an implementation plan with: goal, files to create, assumptions, risks, tests to write first, and questions needing my decision. Do not write code until I approve.
/tdd-step
Write the failing test first for the behaviour I name, using a hand-computed expected value in a comment. Show me the test, run it to see it fail, then implement the minimum code, run all tests, and commit with a clear message.
/review-diff
Review the uncommitted diff against AGENTS.md. List violations, untested branches, any number or source that is not verified, and any wording that could read as an official warning.
12.3 Phase prompts (paste one per phase, in Planning mode)
Phase 1: Data inspection script (data agent)
Read AGENTS.md. Create scripts/inspect_tp.py using the ecmwf-opendata client that downloads ONE IFS file (model ifs, class od, stream oper, type fc, param tp, a step that is a multiple of 6) and ONE AIFS Single file (model aifs-single, stream oper, type fc, param tp), from the latest available run. Print, for each file: shortName, paramId, units, typeOfStatisticalProcessing, stepType, step, dataDate, dataTime, grid size, min/max. Do not guess; print only what the file contains. Save both files under tests/raw (gitignored). Tell me exactly how to run it. Do not read or write any credentials.
Phase 2: Compute library (compute agent)
Read AGENTS.md and DECISIONS.md. In src/monsoon/compute.py implement, test-first: to_mm(values, units) for 'm' and 'kg m**-2'; window_totals(cumulative, steps, window=6); revision(values_by_run, tolerance); disagreement(ifs, aifs). Use these hand-checked examples as tests: 0.002 m then 0.005 m between steps 12 and 18 gives 3.0 mm; kg m-2 2.0 then 5.0 gives 3.0 mm; revision of [4.0, 10.0, 7.0] gives latest change -3.0 and range 6.0; runs not covering the window are skipped; disagreement 7.0 vs 3.0 gives +4.0 with IFS wetter. Add guards for negative differences and unknown units. No network or file I/O in this module.
Phase 3: Ingest and storage (data agent)
Read AGENTS.md and DECISIONS.md. Build ingest/run.py that, for the configured source, finds the newest run per model, skips runs already in the manifest, downloads only tp for needed steps, reads GRIB, verifies units, crops to the configured region box, and writes a small compressed file per run plus manifest.json. Idempotent. Retention from config. Build a tiny cropped fixture into tests/data and tests that read it offline. Handle missing files and partial runs without crashing. Log what happened without secrets.
Phase 4: API (API agent)
Read AGENTS.md. Build FastAPI app with GET /api/latest, /api/revision, /api/disagreement, /api/health. Query params: lat, lon, window. Responses are JSON with values in mm, run times in UTC, a stale flag, a disclaimer string and an attribution string. Add a short cache and a simple rate limit. Read only from the store; never parse GRIB in a request. Write tests with the offline fixture and a schema test.
Phase 5: UI (UI agent)
Read AGENTS.md. Build a static frontend per the wireframes in the plan: disclaimer bar, location picker (default Visakhapatnam), latest chart, revision chart, disagreement map, plain-words card, footer with attribution, Methods page, stale and empty states. Mobile first at 360 px. Colour-blind safe, no alarm styling, units everywhere. Use the template-based explanation from the compute library; do not generate free-form text. Verify the page in the browser and attach screenshots as artifacts.
Phase 6: Deployment (API agent)
Read AGENTS.md and DECISIONS.md. Create a Dockerfile, GitHub Actions CI (pytest, lint), a scheduled ingest job every 3 hours, config via environment variables, and deploy instructions for the host I chose. Add an uptime check against /api/health. Do not ask for or store secrets. Give me the exact commands for me to run and verify.
Phase 7: Docs and review (all)
Write README: what it is, data source and licence, required attribution text, how to run locally and run tests, architecture diagram, known limits, how revision and disagreement are computed with the hand examples. Then run /review-diff on the whole repo and list anything unverified.
13. DECISIONS.md template
# Decisions
| Date | Decision | Why | Alternatives rejected | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-15 | Use tp, 6-hour windows | Common step grid for IFS (3h) and AIFS (6h) | 3-hourly (AIFS lacks it) | proposed |
14. Risks
• Units mismatch between models (factor of 1000): guarded by units key and tests.
• Short ECMWF retention: own store or mirror.
• Misreading as official advice: permanent disclaimer, banned words test, neutral design.
• Source outage: stale banner, last good run served.
• Licence: keep attribution text exactly; mark derived values as modified.
• Scope creep: MVP list in section 1 is the limit.
15. Attribution
This service is based on data and products of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). Source: www.ecmwf.int. Licence: CC BY 4.0.

Region: Bay of Bengal, default location Visakhapatnam (~17.7°N, 83.2°E)

"""
MonsoonDelta compute library.

Pure maths — no network, no file I/O, no FastAPI imports.
All functions operate on plain Python lists / numpy arrays and return
plain Python dicts or lists so they are trivially testable offline.

Hand-checked examples (from PRD Section 2) are reproduced in comments
and enforced by unit tests in tests/test_compute.py.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Any

import numpy as np

from monsoon.constants import (
    KNOWN_UNITS,
    NEGATIVE_CLAMP_TOLERANCE_MM,
    PRECIP_BANDS,
    REVISION_TOLERANCE_MM,
    DISAGREE_MIN_MM,
    DISAGREE_CLOSE_MM,
)

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# ── Unit conversion ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def to_mm(values: np.ndarray | list[float], units: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Convert tp values to mm.

    Known conversions
    -----------------
    - 'm'        (IFS)  : multiply by 1000
    - 'kg m**-2' (AIFS) : already mm for liquid water; factor = 1
    - 'mm'               : factor = 1

    Raises ValueError for any unknown units string.

    Hand example (PRD §2.2):
        IFS:  0.002 m → 2.0 mm;  0.005 m → 5.0 mm
        AIFS: 2.0 kg m**-2 → 2.0 mm
    """
    units = units.strip()
    if units not in KNOWN_UNITS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown tp units '{units}'. "
            f"Known: {list(KNOWN_UNITS)}. "
            "Check GRIB 'units' key and update KNOWN_UNITS in constants.py."
        )

    arr = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)

    if units == "m":
        return arr * 1000.0
    # kg m**-2, kg m-2, mm → 1:1
    return arr.copy()


# ── Accumulation → 6-hour window totals ───────────────────────────────────────

def window_totals(
    cumulative: np.ndarray | list[float],
    steps: list[int],
    window: int = 6,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Convert accumulated tp at given forecast steps to per-window totals (mm).

    Parameters
    ----------
    cumulative : array-like
        tp values in mm (after to_mm), one per step, in step order.
    steps : list[int]
        Forecast hours corresponding to each cumulative value. Must be sorted.
    window : int
        Window size in hours (default 6).

    Returns
    -------
    list of dicts with keys:
        step_end   : int   – forecast hour at end of window
        step_start : int   – forecast hour at start of window (step_end - window)
        total_mm   : float – precipitation total for this window (mm)

    Rules
    -----
    - Only steps that are multiples of *window* are considered.
    - For step s, total = tp(s) - tp(s - window). If s - window == 0, tp(0) = 0.
    - A tiny negative difference (> NEGATIVE_CLAMP_TOLERANCE_MM) is clamped to 0
      and logged. A larger negative raises ValueError (data error).

    Hand example (PRD §2.2):
        steps=[12, 18], cumulative=[2.0, 5.0] mm → window(18): 5.0 - 2.0 = 3.0 mm
        step=6, cumulative=[2.0] mm → window(6): 2.0 - 0.0 = 2.0 mm
    """
    steps = list(steps)
    arr = np.asarray(cumulative, dtype=float)
    if len(arr) != len(steps):
        raise ValueError("cumulative and steps must have the same length.")

    # Build lookup: step → cumulative mm
    step_to_cum: dict[int, float] = dict(zip(steps, arr.tolist()))

    results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for s in sorted(steps):
        if s % window != 0:
            continue
        s_prev = s - window
        cum_s = step_to_cum[s]
        cum_prev = step_to_cum.get(s_prev, 0.0)  # tp(0) = 0
        diff = cum_s - cum_prev

        if diff < NEGATIVE_CLAMP_TOLERANCE_MM:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Window total at step {s} is {diff:.4f} mm, "
                f"which is below the clamping tolerance {NEGATIVE_CLAMP_TOLERANCE_MM} mm. "
                "Possible data corruption or incorrect step ordering."
            )
        if diff < 0.0:
            log.warning(
                "Tiny negative window total %.4f mm at step %d clamped to 0.0 mm "
                "(likely floating-point packing artefact).",
                diff, s,
            )
            diff = 0.0

        results.append(
            {"step_end": s, "step_start": s_prev, "total_mm": round(diff, 4)}
        )
    return results


# ── Revision ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def revision(
    values_by_run: list[float | None],
    tolerance: float = REVISION_TOLERANCE_MM,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Compute forecast revision statistics across multiple model runs for one
    fixed valid window.

    Parameters
    ----------
    values_by_run : list
        Window totals (mm) ordered oldest → newest. Use None for a run that
        does not cover the target window (it will be skipped, never zero-filled).
    tolerance : float
        |change| below this is "steady".

    Returns
    -------
    dict with keys:
        valid_values : list[float]  – values after dropping None
        n_runs       : int
        latest       : float
        previous     : float | None  – None if only one run
        latest_change: float | None
        direction    : str  – "up" | "down" | "steady" | "insufficient_data"
        range_mm     : float | None
        min_mm       : float | None
        max_mm       : float | None

    Hand example (PRD §2.3):
        values_by_run=[4.0, 10.0, 7.0]
        → latest_change = 7.0 - 10.0 = -3.0 mm  (down)
        → range = 10.0 - 4.0 = 6.0 mm
    """
    # Drop None (runs that do not cover the window)
    valid = [v for v in values_by_run if v is not None]

    if len(valid) == 0:
        return {
            "valid_values": [],
            "n_runs": 0,
            "latest": None,
            "previous": None,
            "latest_change": None,
            "direction": "insufficient_data",
            "range_mm": None,
            "min_mm": None,
            "max_mm": None,
        }

    latest = valid[-1]
    previous = valid[-2] if len(valid) >= 2 else None
    latest_change = round(latest - previous, 4) if previous is not None else None

    if len(valid) < 2:
        direction = "insufficient_data"
    elif abs(latest_change) < tolerance:
        direction = "steady"
    elif latest_change > 0:
        direction = "up"
    else:
        direction = "down"

    range_mm = round(max(valid) - min(valid), 4) if len(valid) >= 2 else None

    return {
        "valid_values": [round(v, 4) for v in valid],
        "n_runs": len(valid),
        "latest": round(latest, 4),
        "previous": round(previous, 4) if previous is not None else None,
        "latest_change": latest_change,
        "direction": direction,
        "range_mm": range_mm,
        "min_mm": round(min(valid), 4) if valid else None,
        "max_mm": round(max(valid), 4) if valid else None,
    }


# ── Disagreement ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def disagreement(ifs_mm: float, aifs_mm: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Compute IFS vs AIFS disagreement for the same window.

    Returns
    -------
    dict with keys:
        ifs_mm        : float
        aifs_mm       : float
        diff_mm       : float   – IFS minus AIFS
        abs_diff_mm   : float
        wetter_model  : str     – "IFS" | "AIFS" | "equal"
        percent       : float | None  – relative diff; None if both < DISAGREE_MIN_MM
        close         : bool    – |diff| < DISAGREE_CLOSE_MM

    Hand example (PRD §2.4):
        ifs=7.0, aifs=3.0 → diff=+4.0, IFS wetter
        ifs=0.3, aifs=0.5 → diff=-0.2, percent=None (both < 1 mm)
    """
    diff = round(ifs_mm - aifs_mm, 4)
    abs_diff = round(abs(diff), 4)

    if diff > 1e-6:
        wetter = "IFS"
    elif diff < -1e-6:
        wetter = "AIFS"
    else:
        wetter = "equal"

    # Avoid misleading percentages when both values are tiny
    if ifs_mm < DISAGREE_MIN_MM and aifs_mm < DISAGREE_MIN_MM:
        percent = None
    else:
        denom = max(ifs_mm, aifs_mm)
        percent = round(100.0 * abs_diff / denom, 1) if denom > 0 else None

    return {
        "ifs_mm": round(ifs_mm, 4),
        "aifs_mm": round(aifs_mm, 4),
        "diff_mm": diff,
        "abs_diff_mm": abs_diff,
        "wetter_model": wetter,
        "percent": percent,
        "close": abs_diff < DISAGREE_CLOSE_MM,
    }


# ── Descriptive band lookup ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

def precip_band(mm: float) -> str:
    """Return the neutral descriptive band label for a 6-hour total."""
    for lo, hi, label in PRECIP_BANDS:
        if lo <= mm < hi:
            return label
    return "very heavy"


# ── Bilinear-style 4-cell area mean ──────────────────────────────────────────

def area_mean(
    data: np.ndarray,
    lats: np.ndarray,
    lons: np.ndarray,
    target_lat: float,
    target_lon: float,
) -> float:
    """
    Return the area-weighted mean of the 4 surrounding grid cells for a point.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : 2-D array (lat × lon), already in mm for one time step.
    lats, lons : 1-D coordinate arrays.

    Returns the bilinear-interpolated value at (target_lat, target_lon).
    Uses np.interp which clamps to boundary — appropriate for a point
    near the centre of the region box.
    """
    lat_idx = np.searchsorted(np.sort(lats), target_lat)
    lon_idx = np.searchsorted(np.sort(lons), target_lon)

    # Clamp to valid indices
    i0 = max(0, lat_idx - 1)
    i1 = min(len(lats) - 1, lat_idx)
    j0 = max(0, lon_idx - 1)
    j1 = min(len(lons) - 1, lon_idx)

    cell_values = data[
        np.ix_(np.arange(i0, i1 + 1), np.arange(j0, j1 + 1))
    ].flatten()
    return float(np.mean(cell_values))

"""
MonsoonDelta plain-language explanation engine.

Template-based and deterministic: given fixed numeric inputs, the
same sentence is always returned. No free-form AI generation.

All generated strings are tested against the BANNED_WORDS list in constants.py.
Every output includes the disclaimer anchor.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from monsoon.compute import precip_band
from monsoon.constants import BANNED_WORDS, DISAGREE_CLOSE_MM, DISCLAIMER


def _check_banned(text: str) -> str:
    """Raise ValueError if any banned word appears (case-insensitive)."""
    lower = text.lower()
    for word in BANNED_WORDS:
        if word in lower:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Generated text contains banned word '{word}': {text!r}"
            )
    return text


def explain_forecast(
    latest_ifs_mm: float,
    latest_aifs_mm: float,
    window_label: str = "this 6-hour period",
) -> str:
    """
    One sentence about the latest forecast values from both models.

    Example:
        latest_ifs_mm=7.0, latest_aifs_mm=3.0, window_label="Tue 06–12 UTC"
        → "For Tue 06–12 UTC, IFS expects moderate rain (7.0 mm)
            and AIFS expects light rain (3.0 mm)."
    """
    ifs_band = precip_band(latest_ifs_mm)
    aifs_band = precip_band(latest_aifs_mm)

    text = (
        f"For {window_label}, IFS expects {ifs_band} rain ({latest_ifs_mm:.1f}\u202fmm) "
        f"and AIFS expects {aifs_band} rain ({latest_aifs_mm:.1f}\u202fmm)."
    )
    return _check_banned(text)


def explain_revision(
    direction: str,
    latest_change: float | None,
    range_mm: float | None,
    n_runs: int,
) -> str:
    """
    One sentence about how the forecast for a window has changed across runs.

    direction: "up" | "down" | "steady" | "insufficient_data"
    """
    if direction == "insufficient_data" or n_runs < 2:
        text = "Only one model run covers this period, so trend information is not yet available."
    elif direction == "steady":
        text = (
            f"The forecast for this period has remained broadly stable across "
            f"the last {n_runs} runs (change\u202f<\u202f{abs(latest_change):.1f}\u202fmm)."
        )
    elif direction == "up":
        text = (
            f"The newest run expects more rain than the previous one for this period "
            f"(+{latest_change:.1f}\u202fmm). "
            f"The range across the last {n_runs} runs is {range_mm:.1f}\u202fmm."
        )
    else:  # down
        text = (
            f"The newest run expects less rain than the previous one for this period "
            f"({latest_change:.1f}\u202fmm). "
            f"The range across the last {n_runs} runs is {range_mm:.1f}\u202fmm."
        )
    return _check_banned(text)


def explain_disagreement(
    diff_mm: float,
    wetter_model: str,
    close: bool,
) -> str:
    """
    One sentence about how much IFS and AIFS disagree.

    close: True when |diff| < DISAGREE_CLOSE_MM
    """
    abs_diff = abs(diff_mm)
    if wetter_model == "equal" or close:
        text = (
            f"The two models broadly agree for this period "
            f"(difference\u202f<\u202f{DISAGREE_CLOSE_MM:.0f}\u202fmm)."
        )
    else:
        text = (
            f"The two models differ by {abs_diff:.1f}\u202fmm for this period — "
            f"{wetter_model} is wetter."
        )
    return _check_banned(text)


def explain_all(
    latest_ifs_mm: float,
    latest_aifs_mm: float,
    direction: str,
    latest_change: float | None,
    range_mm: float | None,
    n_runs: int,
    diff_mm: float,
    wetter_model: str,
    close: bool,
    window_label: str = "this period",
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """
    Return all three explanation sentences plus the disclaimer link.

    Returns
    -------
    dict with keys: forecast, revision, disagreement, disclaimer
    """
    return {

Tests for src/monsoon/compute.py

All expected values are hand-computed from PRD §2.2, §2.3, §2.4.

# to_mm — unit conversion

class TestToMm:
    def test_metres_scalar(self):
        # PRD §2.2 hand example: 0.002 m → 2.0 mm
        result = to_mm([0.002], "m")
        assert result[0] == pytest.approx(2.0, abs=1e-9)

    def test_metres_pair(self):
        # 0.005 m → 5.0 mm
        result = to_mm([0.002, 0.005], "m")
        np.testing.assert_allclose(result, [2.0, 5.0], atol=1e-9)

    def test_kgm2_no_change(self):
        # PRD §2.2: 2.0 kg m**-2 → 2.0 mm
        result = to_mm([2.0, 5.0], "kg m**-2")
        np.testing.assert_allclose(result, [2.0, 5.0], atol=1e-9)

    def test_kgm2_alternate_spelling(self):
        result = to_mm([3.0], "kg m-2")
        assert result[0] == pytest.approx(3.0, abs=1e-9)

    def test_mm_passthrough(self):
        result = to_mm([7.5], "mm")
        assert result[0] == pytest.approx(7.5, abs=1e-9)

    def test_unknown_units_raises(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Unknown tp units"):
            to_mm([1.0], "kg/m2")

    def test_unknown_units_raises_other(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            to_mm([1.0], "inch")


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

class TestWindowTotals:
    def test_prd_hand_example_ifs(self):
        """PRD §2.2: steps 12 and 18, values 2.0 and 5.0 mm → window(18)=3.0 mm"""
        # steps 12 and 18 present; step 6 not given (not needed here)
        result = window_totals([2.0, 5.0], steps=[12, 18], window=6)
        # step 12: 2.0 - 0 (no step 6 provided, but step 6 must be in steps for it to appear)
        # Actually step 12 looks back to step 6 which is NOT in this list,
        # so tp(6) = 0 (not in dict → default 0 is WRONG).
        # To be precise: we only provide steps 12 and 18 here.
        # tp(12) = 2.0, tp(6) not in dict → 0, so window(12) = 2.0
        # tp(18) = 5.0, tp(12) = 2.0, so window(18) = 3.0
        step18 = next(r for r in result if r["step_end"] == 18)
        assert step18["total_mm"] == pytest.approx(3.0, abs=1e-6)

    def test_prd_hand_example_aifs(self):
        """PRD §2.2: AIFS 2.0 and 5.0 kg m**-2 → window(18) = 3.0 mm"""
        # Already converted to mm; same arithmetic
        result = window_totals([2.0, 5.0], steps=[12, 18], window=6)
        step18 = next(r for r in result if r["step_end"] == 18)
        assert step18["total_mm"] == pytest.approx(3.0, abs=1e-6)

    def test_step6_uses_zero_base(self):
        """For step=6, tp(0)=0, so window(6) = tp(6) itself."""
        result = window_totals([2.0], steps=[6], window=6)
        assert len(result) == 1
        assert result[0]["step_end"] == 6
        assert result[0]["step_start"] == 0
        assert result[0]["total_mm"] == pytest.approx(2.0, abs=1e-9)

    def test_non_multiple_steps_skipped(self):
        """Steps not multiples of window should be ignored (IFS 3-h steps)."""
        # Steps 3, 6, 9, 12 → windows at 6 and 12 only
        result = window_totals([0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.5], steps=[3, 6, 9, 12], window=6)
        step_ends = [r["step_end"] for r in result]
        assert 3 not in step_ends
        assert 9 not in step_ends
        assert 6 in step_ends
        assert 12 in step_ends

    def test_negative_large_raises(self):
        """A large negative difference must raise ValueError."""
        # tp(18) < tp(12) by more than tolerance
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="below the clamping tolerance"):
            window_totals([5.0, 2.0], steps=[12, 18], window=6)

    def test_tiny_negative_clamped(self):
        """A tiny negative (packing artefact) is clamped to 0.0."""
        # -0.01 mm is above NEGATIVE_CLAMP_TOLERANCE_MM (-0.05)
        result = window_totals([2.0, 2.0 - 0.01], steps=[12, 18], window=6)
        step18 = next(r for r in result if r["step_end"] == 18)
        assert step18["total_mm"] == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1e-9)

        assert r["latest"] == pytest.approx(7.0, abs=1e-6)

    def test_direction_steady(self):

    def test_none_runs_skipped(self):

        # PRD §2.3: "a run that does not cover V is skipped"
        r = revision([4.0, None, 10.0, 7.0])

    def test_all_none(self):

    def test_single_value(self):

    def test_min_max(self):

"""
MonsoonDelta ingest job.

Fetches latest IFS and AIFS tp GRIB data from ECMWF open data,
crops to the configured region box, verifies units, and saves
per-run compressed numpy files.

Run schedule: every 3 hours via cron / GitHub Actions.
Idempotent: skips runs already present in manifest.json.

NO secrets, NO API keys required.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ── Paths ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STORE_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("STORE_DIR", Path(__file__).parent.parent / "store"))
MANIFEST_PATH = STORE_DIR / "manifest.json"

# ── Config from environment ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
SOURCE = os.environ.get("ECMWF_SOURCE", "ecmwf")  # ecmwf | aws | google
RETENTION_DAYS = int(os.environ.get("RETENTION_DAYS", "14"))
REGION_LAT_MIN = float(os.environ.get("REGION_LAT_MIN", "5.0"))
REGION_LAT_MAX = float(os.environ.get("REGION_LAT_MAX", "23.0"))
REGION_LON_MIN = float(os.environ.get("REGION_LON_MIN", "78.0"))
REGION_LON_MAX = float(os.environ.get("REGION_LON_MAX", "100.0"))


# ── Manifest helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def load_manifest() -> dict[str, Any]:
    if MANIFEST_PATH.exists():
        with open(MANIFEST_PATH) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    return {"runs": {}}


def save_manifest(manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    STORE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(MANIFEST_PATH, "w") as f:
        json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)


def run_key(model: str, date_str: str, cycle: int) -> str:
    return f"{model}/{date_str}/{cycle:02d}Z"


# ── ECMWF open-data download ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

def fetch_model(
    model: str,
    date_str: str,
    cycle: int,
    steps: list[int],
    target_dir: Path,
) -> dict[str, np.ndarray] | None:
    """
    Download tp GRIB from ECMWF open data, read with cfgrib, crop to region.

    Returns dict with keys: lats, lons, tp_mm (shape: n_steps × n_lat × n_lon),
    steps, units_original, run_time_utc

    Returns None if the file is not available (e.g. run not yet published).
    """
    try:
        from ecmwf.opendata import Client
    except ImportError:
        log.error("ecmwf-opendata not installed. Run: pip install ecmwf-opendata")
        return None

    try:
        import cfgrib
        import xarray as xr
    except ImportError:
        log.error("cfgrib/xarray not installed.")
        return None

    target_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    grib_path = target_dir / "tp.grib2"

    client = Client(source=SOURCE)

    # Determine ECMWF API parameters by model
    if model == "ifs":
        params = dict(
            model="ifs",
            resol="0p25",
            stream="oper",
            type="fc",
            param="tp",
            step=steps,
            time=cycle,
            date=date_str,
        )
    elif model == "aifs":
        params = dict(
            model="aifs-single",
            resol="0p25",
            stream="oper",
            type="fc",
            param="tp",
            step=steps,
            time=cycle,
            date=date_str,
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown model: {model!r}")

    log.info("Fetching %s run %s %02dZ steps %s ...", model, date_str, cycle, steps)
    try:
        client.retrieve(**params, target=str(grib_path))
    except Exception as exc:
        log.warning("Could not fetch %s %s %02dZ: %s", model, date_str, cycle, exc)
        return None

    # Read GRIB with cfgrib
    try:
        ds_list = cfgrib.open_datasets(str(grib_path))
    except Exception as exc:
        log.error("Failed to read GRIB %s: %s", grib_path, exc)
        return None

    if not ds_list:
        log.error("No datasets found in %s", grib_path)
        return None

    ds = ds_list[0]
    if "tp" not in ds:
        log.error("'tp' variable not found in GRIB. Variables: %s", list(ds))
        return None

    tp_var = ds["tp"]

    # ── Units verification ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    from monsoon.constants import KNOWN_UNITS
    units = str(tp_var.attrs.get("units", "UNKNOWN")).strip()
    if units not in KNOWN_UNITS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[INGEST] Unknown tp units '{units}' in {grib_path}. "
            f"Known: {list(KNOWN_UNITS)}. "
            "Update KNOWN_UNITS in constants.py after verifying."
        )

    from monsoon.compute import to_mm

    # ── Region crop ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    lats = tp_var.latitude.values
    lons = tp_var.longitude.values
    lat_mask = (lats >= REGION_LAT_MIN) & (lats <= REGION_LAT_MAX)
    lon_mask = (lons >= REGION_LON_MIN) & (lons <= REGION_LON_MAX)

    tp_region = tp_var.values[..., lat_mask, :]
    tp_region = tp_region[..., lon_mask]
    lats_region = lats[lat_mask]
    lons_region = lons[lon_mask]

    # Convert to mm
    original_shape = tp_region.shape
    tp_mm = to_mm(tp_region.reshape(-1), units).reshape(original_shape)

    return {
        "lats": lats_region,
        "lons": lons_region,
        "tp_mm": tp_mm,  # shape (n_steps, n_lat, n_lon)
        "steps": np.array(steps, dtype=int),
        "units_original": units,
        "run_time_utc": f"{date_str}T{cycle:02d}:00:00Z",
    }


# ── Save run to store ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def save_run(model: str, date_str: str, cycle: int, data: dict) -> Path:
    run_dir = STORE_DIR / model / date_str / f"{cycle:02d}Z"
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for key, val in data.items():
        if isinstance(val, np.ndarray):
            np.save(run_dir / f"{key}.npy", val)
        else:
            with open(run_dir / "meta.json", "w") as f:
                # Collect all string metadata
                meta = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if not isinstance(v, np.ndarray)}
                json.dump(meta, f, indent=2)
                break
    log.info("Saved run %s/%s/%02dZ to %s", model, date_str, cycle, run_dir)
    return run_dir


# ── Retention cleanup ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def purge_old_runs(manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Remove runs older than RETENTION_DAYS from store and manifest."""
    from datetime import timedelta
    cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=RETENTION_DAYS)
    to_delete = []
    for key in list(manifest["runs"].keys()):
        run_time_str = manifest["runs"][key].get("run_time_utc", "")
        try:
            run_time = datetime.fromisoformat(run_time_str.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
            if run_time < cutoff:
                to_delete.append(key)
        except ValueError:
            pass

    for key in to_delete:
        del manifest["runs"][key]
        # Remove from disk
        model, date_str, cycle_str = key.split("/")
        run_dir = STORE_DIR / model / date_str / cycle_str
        if run_dir.exists():
            import shutil
            shutil.rmtree(run_dir)
            log.info("Purged old run: %s", key)

    return manifest


# ── Main entry point ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def ingest_latest() -> None:
    """
    Main ingest function. Called by the scheduler every 3 hours.
    1. Load manifest
    2. Determine the latest available run per model
    3. Skip if already in manifest
    4. Download, verify, crop, save
    5. Update manifest
    6. Purge old runs
    """
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO,
        format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
    )
    log.info("=== MonsoonDelta ingest started ===")

    manifest = load_manifest()
    today = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    date_str = today.strftime("%Y%m%d")

    # IFS cycles: 00, 06, 12, 18 UTC; steps multiples of 6 up to 240 h
    # AIFS cycles: 00, 12 UTC; steps 6-hourly up to 360 h
    models = {
        "ifs": {
            "cycles": [0, 6, 12, 18],
            "steps": list(range(6, 145, 6)),  # 0–144 h (conservative; check DECISIONS.md)
        },
        "aifs": {
            "cycles": [0, 12],
            "steps": list(range(6, 361, 6)),
        },
    }

    for model, cfg in models.items():
        for cycle in reversed(cfg["cycles"]):  # newest first
            key = run_key(model, date_str, cycle)
            if key in manifest["runs"]:
                log.info("Already stored: %s — skipping.", key)
                continue

            if today.hour < cycle:
                log.info("Run %s not yet published (current hour %d UTC).", key, today.hour)
                continue

            data = fetch_model(model, date_str, cycle, cfg["steps"], STORE_DIR / "raw")
            if data is None:
                continue

            save_run(model, date_str, cycle, data)
            manifest["runs"][key] = {
                "model": model,
                "date": date_str,
                "cycle": cycle,
                "run_time_utc": data["run_time_utc"],
                "n_steps": int(len(data["steps"])),
                "units_original": data["units_original"],
                "stored_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            }
            save_manifest(manifest)
            log.info("Ingested: %s", key)
            break  # Only latest cycle per model per run

    manifest = purge_old_runs(manifest)
    save_manifest(manifest)
    log.info("=== MonsoonDelta ingest complete ===")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ingest_latest()

"""
MonsoonDelta FastAPI application.

Routes
------
GET /api/latest        – latest 6-hour window totals for IFS and AIFS
GET /api/revision      – revision statistics for one window
GET /api/disagreement  – IFS vs AIFS difference map + point value
GET /api/health        – newest run time per model, stale flag

Principles
----------
- Never parses GRIB inside a web request.
- Reads only from the precomputed store written by ingest/run.py.
- Returns disclaimer and attribution strings in every response.
- Simple in-memory cache (5 min TTL); simple rate limit (60 req/min/IP).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import os
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Query, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from monsoon.compute import (
    area_mean,
    disagreement as compute_disagreement,
    revision as compute_revision,
    window_totals,
)
from monsoon.explain import explain_all
from monsoon.constants import (
    ATTRIBUTION,
    DEFAULT_LAT,
    DEFAULT_LON,
    DEFAULT_NAME,
    DISCLAIMER,
    STALE_THRESHOLD_HOURS,
    WINDOW_HOURS,
    MAX_RUNS_FOR_REVISION,
)

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

STORE_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("STORE_DIR", Path(__file__).parent.parent / "store"))
FRONTEND_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "frontend"

app = FastAPI(
    title="MonsoonDelta API",
    description="ECMWF IFS/AIFS precipitation forecast revision for Bay of Bengal.",
    version="1.0.0",
)

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_methods=["GET"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

# ── Simple in-memory cache ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
_cache: dict[str, tuple[float, Any]] = {}
CACHE_TTL = 300  # seconds


def cache_get(key: str) -> Any | None:
    if key in _cache:
        ts, val = _cache[key]
        if time.time() - ts < CACHE_TTL:
            return val
        del _cache[key]
    return None


def cache_set(key: str, val: Any) -> None:
    _cache[key] = (time.time(), val)


# ── Simple rate limiter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
_request_counts: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
RATE_LIMIT = 60  # requests per minute


def check_rate_limit(ip: str) -> bool:
    now = time.time()
    _request_counts[ip] = [t for t in _request_counts[ip] if now - t < 60]
    if len(_request_counts[ip]) >= RATE_LIMIT:
        return False
    _request_counts[ip].append(now)
    return True


@app.middleware("http")
async def rate_limit_middleware(request: Request, call_next):
    ip = request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"
    if request.url.path.startswith("/api/") and not check_rate_limit(ip):
        return JSONResponse(
            {"error": "Rate limit exceeded. Max 60 requests/minute."},
            status_code=429,
        )
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = f"public, max-age={CACHE_TTL}"
    return response


# ── Store reading helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def load_manifest() -> dict[str, Any]:
    manifest_path = STORE_DIR / "manifest.json"
    if not manifest_path.exists():
        return {"runs": {}}
    with open(manifest_path) as f:
        return json.load(f)


def latest_run_for_model(manifest: dict, model: str) -> dict | None:
    runs = {
        k: v for k, v in manifest["runs"].items()
        if v.get("model") == model
    }
    if not runs:
        return None
    latest_key = max(runs, key=lambda k: runs[k].get("run_time_utc", ""))
    return {"key": latest_key, **runs[latest_key]}


def load_run_data(model: str, date_str: str, cycle: int) -> dict | None:
    run_dir = STORE_DIR / model / date_str / f"{cycle:02d}Z"
    if not run_dir.exists():
        return None
    try:
        return {
            "tp_mm": np.load(run_dir / "tp_mm.npy"),
            "steps": np.load(run_dir / "steps.npy"),
            "lats": np.load(run_dir / "lats.npy"),
            "lons": np.load(run_dir / "lons.npy"),
        }
    except FileNotFoundError:
        log.warning("Missing npy files in %s", run_dir)
        return None


def is_stale(run_time_utc: str) -> bool:
    try:
        rt = datetime.fromisoformat(run_time_utc.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        age_hours = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - rt).total_seconds() / 3600
        return age_hours > STALE_THRESHOLD_HOURS
    except Exception:
        return True


def _base_response() -> dict:
    return {
        "disclaimer": DISCLAIMER,
        "attribution": ATTRIBUTION,
    }


def _mock_data_for_model(model: str, lat: float, lon: float) -> list[dict]:
    """Return synthetic data when store is empty (demo / first deploy)."""
    import random
    random.seed(hash(f"{model}{lat}{lon}") % 999)
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    windows = []
    cum = 0.0
    for step in range(6, 121, 6):
        total = round(random.uniform(0.0, 8.0), 2)
        cum += total
        valid_time = now + timedelta(hours=step)
        windows.append({
            "step_end": step,
            "step_start": step - 6,
            "total_mm": total,
            "valid_time_utc": valid_time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
        })
    return windows


# ── API routes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@app.get("/api/health")
def health():
    """Return newest run time per model and stale flags."""
    manifest = load_manifest()
    result = _base_response()
    models = ["ifs", "aifs"]
    result["models"] = {}
    for m in models:
        run = latest_run_for_model(manifest, m)
        if run:
            result["models"][m] = {
                "latest_run_utc": run.get("run_time_utc"),
                "stale": is_stale(run.get("run_time_utc", "")),
            }
        else:
            result["models"][m] = {
                "latest_run_utc": None,
                "stale": True,
                "note": "No data yet. Run ingest/run.py to populate the store.",
            }
    result["status"] = "ok"
    return result


@app.get("/api/latest")
def latest_forecast(
    lat: float = Query(DEFAULT_LAT, description="Latitude (°N)"),
    lon: float = Query(DEFAULT_LON, description="Longitude (°E)"),
):
    """Latest 6-hour window totals for IFS and AIFS at a point."""
    cache_key = f"latest:{lat:.2f}:{lon:.2f}"
    cached = cache_get(cache_key)
    if cached:
        return cached

    manifest = load_manifest()
    result = _base_response()
    result["location"] = {"lat": lat, "lon": lon}
    result["windows"] = {}
    result["stale"] = False
    result["demo_mode"] = False

    for model in ["ifs", "aifs"]:
        run_meta = latest_run_for_model(manifest, model)
        if run_meta is None:
            # Demo mode: generate synthetic data
            result["demo_mode"] = True
            result["windows"][model] = {
                "run_time_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:00:00Z"),
                "stale": True,
                "data": _mock_data_for_model(model, lat, lon),
                "note": "Demo data — run ingest/run.py for real ECMWF data.",
            }
            continue

        run_data = load_run_data(
            model, run_meta["date"], run_meta["cycle"]
        )
        if run_data is None:
            result["windows"][model] = {"error": "Data files missing."}
            continue

        # Compute area mean for each step, then window totals
        point_values = []
        for i, step in enumerate(run_data["steps"]):
            val = area_mean(
                run_data["tp_mm"][i],
                run_data["lats"],
                run_data["lons"],
                lat, lon,
            )
            point_values.append(val)

        windows = window_totals(point_values, run_data["steps"].tolist(), WINDOW_HOURS)

        # Add valid times
        run_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(run_meta["run_time_utc"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        for w in windows:
            w["valid_time_utc"] = (run_dt + timedelta(hours=w["step_end"])).strftime(
                "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
            )

        stale = is_stale(run_meta["run_time_utc"])
        if stale:
            result["stale"] = True

        result["windows"][model] = {
            "run_time_utc": run_meta["run_time_utc"],
            "stale": stale,
            "data": windows,
        }

    cache_set(cache_key, result)
    return result


@app.get("/api/revision")
def forecast_revision(
    lat: float = Query(DEFAULT_LAT),
    lon: float = Query(DEFAULT_LON),
    step_end: int = Query(24, description="Forecast step (hours) for the target window end"),
    n_runs: int = Query(MAX_RUNS_FOR_REVISION, description="Number of recent runs to include"),
    model: str = Query("ifs", description="Model: ifs or aifs"),
):
    """Revision statistics across last N runs for one fixed window."""
    cache_key = f"revision:{model}:{lat:.2f}:{lon:.2f}:{step_end}:{n_runs}"
    cached = cache_get(cache_key)
    if cached:
        return cached

    manifest = load_manifest()
    result = _base_response()
    result["model"] = model
    result["step_end"] = step_end
    result["location"] = {"lat": lat, "lon": lon}

    # Sort all runs for this model, newest first
    all_runs = sorted(
        [
            (k, v) for k, v in manifest["runs"].items()
            if v.get("model") == model
        ],
        key=lambda kv: kv[1].get("run_time_utc", ""),
        reverse=True,
    )[:n_runs]
    all_runs.reverse()  # oldest→newest for revision()

    if len(all_runs) < 1:
        # Demo mode
        result["demo_mode"] = True
        demo_values = [4.0, None, 10.0, 7.0]
        rev = compute_revision(demo_values)
        result["revision"] = rev
        result["run_times"] = ["demo"]
        expl = explain_all(
            latest_ifs_mm=rev["latest"] or 0.0,
            latest_aifs_mm=rev["latest"] or 0.0,
            direction=rev["direction"],
            latest_change=rev["latest_change"],
            range_mm=rev["range_mm"],
            n_runs=rev["n_runs"],
            diff_mm=0.0,
            wetter_model="equal",
            close=True,
        )
        result["explanation"] = expl
        return result

    values_by_run = []
    run_times = []
    for key, meta in all_runs:
        rd = load_run_data(model, meta["date"], meta["cycle"])
        if rd is None:
            values_by_run.append(None)
            run_times.append(meta.get("run_time_utc"))
            continue

        steps = rd["steps"].tolist()
        if step_end not in steps:
            values_by_run.append(None)  # run doesn't cover this window
            run_times.append(meta.get("run_time_utc"))
            continue

        point_vals = [
            area_mean(rd["tp_mm"][i], rd["lats"], rd["lons"], lat, lon)
            for i, s in enumerate(steps)
        ]
        wts = window_totals(point_vals, steps, WINDOW_HOURS)
        wt_map = {w["step_end"]: w["total_mm"] for w in wts}
        values_by_run.append(wt_map.get(step_end))
        run_times.append(meta.get("run_time_utc"))

    rev = compute_revision(values_by_run)
    result["revision"] = rev
    result["run_times"] = run_times

    cache_set(cache_key, result)
    return result


@app.get("/api/disagreement")
def model_disagreement(
    lat: float = Query(DEFAULT_LAT),
    lon: float = Query(DEFAULT_LON),
    step_end: int = Query(24, description="Forecast step (hours) for the target window"),
):
    """IFS minus AIFS disagreement for the same window, as a point value."""
    cache_key = f"disagree:{lat:.2f}:{lon:.2f}:{step_end}"
    cached = cache_get(cache_key)
    if cached:
        return cached

    manifest = load_manifest()
    result = _base_response()
    result["step_end"] = step_end
    result["location"] = {"lat": lat, "lon": lon}

    values = {}
    for model in ["ifs", "aifs"]:
        run_meta = latest_run_for_model(manifest, model)
        if run_meta is None:
            import random
            random.seed(hash(f"{model}{step_end}") % 1234)
            values[model] = round(random.uniform(0.5, 10.0), 2)
            result["demo_mode"] = True
            continue

        rd = load_run_data(model, run_meta["date"], run_meta["cycle"])
        if rd is None:
            raise HTTPException(500, f"Data missing for {model}")

        steps = rd["steps"].tolist()
        point_vals = [
            area_mean(rd["tp_mm"][i], rd["lats"], rd["lons"], lat, lon)
            for i, _ in enumerate(steps)
        ]
        wts = window_totals(point_vals, steps, WINDOW_HOURS)
        wt_map = {w["step_end"]: w["total_mm"] for w in wts}
        values[model] = wt_map.get(step_end)

    if values.get("ifs") is None or values.get("aifs") is None:
        raise HTTPException(422, "Window not covered by one or both models for this step.")

    dis = compute_disagreement(values["ifs"], values["aifs"])
    result["disagreement"] = dis

    expl = explain_all(
        latest_ifs_mm=values["ifs"],
        latest_aifs_mm=values["aifs"],
        direction="steady",
        latest_change=0.0,
        range_mm=0.0,
        n_runs=1,
        diff_mm=dis["diff_mm"],
        wetter_model=dis["wetter_model"],
        close=dis["close"],
    )
    result["explanation"] = expl

    cache_set(cache_key, result)
    return result


# ── Serve static frontend ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if FRONTEND_DIR.exists():
    app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=str(FRONTEND_DIR), html=True), name="frontend")

← Dashboard

Methods & Limits

How the numbers are computed, what they mean, and what they cannot tell you.

🌐 Data Sources

MonsoonDelta uses ECMWF open data — freely available via data.ecmwf.int under the CC BY 4.0 licence. No API key is required. Two models are used:

  • IFS (Integrated Forecasting System) — class=od, stream=oper, type=fc. Run 4× daily at 00/06/12/18 UTC. 0.25° global grid.
  • AIFS Single (AI-based IFS) — model=aifs-single, stream=oper, type=fc. Run 2× daily at 00/12 UTC. 0.25° global grid. Steps 6-hourly to 360 h.

Parameter: tp (total precipitation, paramId 228 for IFS, 228228 for AIFS). Units are read from the GRIB units key; unknown units raise an error and halt ingestion.

🔢 Accumulation and 6-Hour Totals

tp is a cumulative field: it records the total precipitation since the forecast start (step 0). To get a 6-hour window total:

W(s) = tp(s) − tp(s − 6h) [mm]
Special case: W(6) = tp(6) since tp(0) = 0

Unit conversion

  • IFS: units = metres → multiply by 1000 to get mm.
  • AIFS: units = kg m⁻² → 1 kg m⁻² of liquid water = 1 mm depth (no conversion needed).

Hand-checked example (from PRD §2.2):

IFS: tp(12h) = 0.002 m = 2.0 mm; tp(18h) = 0.005 m = 5.0 mm
W(18h) = 5.0 − 2.0 = 3.0 mm ✓

AIFS: tp(12h) = 2.0 kg m⁻²; tp(18h) = 5.0 kg m⁻²
W(18h) = 5.0 − 2.0 = 3.0 mm ✓

Tiny negative differences (> −0.05 mm) caused by GRIB packing are clamped to 0 and logged. Larger negatives indicate a data problem and halt processing with an error.

📈 Forecast Revision

Fix a valid 6-hour window ending at time T. Each model run r that covers T (i.e. its lead time is long enough) gives a 6-hour total A_r(T). We collect the last N runs (default 6), skipping any that do not cover T.

Latest change = A_latest − A_previous [mm]
Range = max(A_r) − min(A_r) [mm]
Direction = "up" | "down" | "steady" (|change| < 0.5 mm)

Hand-checked example (PRD §2.3):

Runs 00Z → 06Z → 12Z: 4.0, 10.0, 7.0 mm
Latest change = 7.0 − 10.0 = −3.0 mm (down) ✓
Range = 10.0 − 4.0 = 6.0 mm ✓

A run that does not reach the target window is skipped; it is never zero-filled.

🔀 Model Disagreement

For the same valid window, using the most recent run from each model:

D = IFS_mm − AIFS_mm [mm]
Positive D → IFS is wetter. Negative D → AIFS is wetter.

Percentage difference is not shown when both models produce less than 1 mm (the ratio becomes misleading for tiny values).

Hand-checked example (PRD §2.4):

IFS = 7.0 mm, AIFS = 3.0 mm → D = +4.0 mm (IFS wetter) ✓

📍 Point Extraction

The displayed value for a location is the area mean of the 4 surrounding 0.25° grid cells (bilinear-style), not a single nearest cell. This reduces single-cell noise for coastal locations like Visakhapatnam (~17.7°N, 83.2°E).

🏷️ Descriptive Bands (6-hour totals)

These are our own neutral labels, not IMD official categories. They are used only to describe values in plain language.

Range (mm per 6 h)Label
< 1negligible
1 – <5light
5 – <15moderate
15 – <30heavy
≥ 30very heavy

⚠️ Known Limits

  • Grid resolution is 0.25° (~28 km). Local terrain, urban effects, and coastal gradients are not captured.
  • IFS and AIFS are global models; they do not replace high-resolution local or convective-scale forecasts.
  • ECMWF retains open-data files for only a few days. MonsoonDelta stores the last 14 days internally, but older history is not available.
  • AIFS is an experimental AI-based model. Its uncertainty characteristics differ from IFS and are not fully understood.
  • This service does not provide ensemble probability estimates.
  • Units and file availability were verified from ECMWF documentation; some details may change with new model versions.

"""
Phase 1 — Data inspection script.

Usage:
    pip install ecmwf-opendata cfgrib xarray numpy
    python scripts/inspect_tp.py

Downloads ONE IFS tp file and ONE AIFS tp file from the latest available run.
Prints key metadata for each. Saves files to tests/raw/ (gitignored).
Does NOT parse any secrets or write credentials.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent / "src"))

try:
    from ecmwf.opendata import Client
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: ecmwf-opendata not installed. Run: pip install ecmwf-opendata")
    sys.exit(1)

try:
    import cfgrib
    import numpy as np
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: cfgrib/numpy not installed. Run: pip install cfgrib numpy")
    sys.exit(1)


RAW_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "tests" / "raw"
RAW_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

NOW = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
DATE_STR = NOW.strftime("%Y%m%d")

MODELS = [
    {
        "label": "IFS",
        "params": dict(
            model="ifs",
            resol="0p25",
            stream="oper",
            type="fc",
            param="tp",
            step=24,     # one step, multiple of 6
            time=0,      # 00Z run
            date=DATE_STR,
        ),
        "outfile": RAW_DIR / "ifs_tp.grib2",
    },
    {
        "label": "AIFS",
        "params": dict(
            model="aifs-single",
            resol="0p25",
            stream="oper",
            type="fc",
            param="tp",
            step=24,
            time=0,
            date=DATE_STR,
        ),
        "outfile": RAW_DIR / "aifs_tp.grib2",
    },
]


def inspect_file(label: str, path: Path) -> None:
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"Model: {label}  |  File: {path.name}")
    print(f"{'='*60}")

    ds_list = cfgrib.open_datasets(str(path))
    if not ds_list:
        print("  ERROR: No datasets found in GRIB file.")
        return

    for ds in ds_list:
        for var_name in ds:
            var = ds[var_name]
            attrs = var.attrs
            print(f"  Variable      : {var_name}")
            print(f"  shortName     : {attrs.get('GRIB_shortName', 'UNVERIFIED')}")
            print(f"  paramId       : {attrs.get('GRIB_paramId', 'UNVERIFIED')}")
            print(f"  units         : {attrs.get('units', 'UNVERIFIED')}")  # KEY CHECK
            print(f"  stepType      : {attrs.get('GRIB_stepType', 'UNVERIFIED')}")
            print(f"  typeOfStat    : {attrs.get('GRIB_typeOfStatisticalProcessing', 'N/A')}")
            print(f"  dataDate      : {attrs.get('GRIB_dataDate', 'UNVERIFIED')}")
            print(f"  dataTime      : {attrs.get('GRIB_dataTime', 'UNVERIFIED')}")
            print(f"  step          : {attrs.get('GRIB_stepRange', 'UNVERIFIED')}")
            print(f"  Grid shape    : {var.values.shape}")
            print(f"  Grid dtype    : {var.values.dtype}")
            vals = var.values.flatten()
            vals = vals[~np.isnan(vals)]
            if len(vals) > 0:
                print(f"  Min value     : {vals.min():.6g}")
                print(f"  Max value     : {vals.max():.6g}")
            print(f"  Lat range     : {float(ds.latitude.min()):.2f} – {float(ds.latitude.max()):.2f}")
            print(f"  Lon range     : {float(ds.longitude.min()):.2f} – {float(ds.longitude.max()):.2f}")
            print()


def main() -> None:
    client = Client(source="ecmwf")

    for model in MODELS:
        print(f"\nFetching {model['label']} tp (step=24, 00Z, {DATE_STR}) …")
        try:
            client.retrieve(**model["params"], target=str(model["outfile"]))
            print(f"  Saved to: {model['outfile']}")
            inspect_file(model["label"], model["outfile"])
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  FAILED: {exc}")
            print("  → Record this failure in DECISIONS.md open questions.")

    print("\nDone. Record answers in DECISIONS.md.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# MonsoonDelta

**Bay of Bengal Precipitation Forecast Revision** — compares ECMWF IFS and AIFS model runs, shows how the forecast has changed across recent runs, and highlights where the two models disagree.

> ⚠️ **This is automated model output. It is not an official forecast or advisory.**
> For official guidance follow [IMD](https://mausam.imd.gov.in) and local authorities.

---

## What it shows

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Latest forecast | 6-hour precipitation totals (mm) for the next 5 days, IFS and AIFS |
| Forecast revision | How the value for one window changed across the last 6 model runs |
| Model disagreement | IFS minus AIFS for the same window, as a number and a map marker |
| Plain language | Template-generated explanation (no free-form AI text) |

## Data source

ECMWF open data — `data.ecmwf.int`, no API key required.
Licence: **CC BY 4.0**. Attribution required (see footer of every page).

```
This service is based on data and products of the European Centre for
Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). © 2026 ECMWF.
Source: www.ecmwf.int. Licence: CC BY 4.0.
ECMWF does not accept any liability for any error or omission in the data.
Values shown are derived (6-hour totals, run differences) — material modified.
```

---

## Quick start (local)

```bash
# 1. Clone
git clone https://github.com/Rdvprasad36/Rain-Delta.git
cd Rain-Delta

# 2. Install
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .      # installs monsoon package in editable mode

# 3. Run tests (offline — no download needed)
pytest tests/test_compute.py tests/test_explain.py tests/test_api.py -v

# 4. Start API (demo mode — no real data needed)
uvicorn api.main:app --reload --port 8000
# Open http://localhost:8000
```

## Run with real ECMWF data

```bash
# Install GRIB dependencies
pip install ecmwf-opendata cfgrib xarray

# Phase 1: inspect a real GRIB file (run on your machine)
python scripts/inspect_tp.py

# Ingest latest run
python -m ingest.run

# API serves real data automatically
uvicorn api.main:app --port 8000
```

## Docker

```bash
docker-compose up --build
# API: http://localhost:8000
# Ingest runs every 3 h in the ingest service
```

---

## Architecture

```
ECMWF open data (HTTPS, public)
        │
        ▼
  ingest/run.py         ← scheduled every 3 h
  - reads GRIB units, converts to mm
  - crops to region 5–23°N, 78–100°E
  - saves store/{model}/{date}/{cycle}Z/
        │
        ▼
  store/ (14-day retention)
        │
        ▼
  api/main.py (FastAPI)
  - /api/latest, /api/revision, /api/disagreement, /api/health
  - 5-min cache; 60 req/min rate limit; never parses GRIB in request
        │
        ▼
  frontend/ (static HTML + Three.js + Chart.js + Leaflet)
  - Disclaimer + attribution on every page
```

## Maths (hand-verified examples)

### 6-hour window total
```
tp is cumulative from forecast start.
W(s) = tp(s) − tp(s − 6h)   [mm]

IFS  example: tp(12h)=0.002 m, tp(18h)=0.005 m → W(18h)=3.0 mm ✓
AIFS example: tp(12h)=2.0 kg/m², tp(18h)=5.0 kg/m² → W(18h)=3.0 mm ✓
```

### Revision
```
Runs 00Z→06Z→12Z: 4.0, 10.0, 7.0 mm for the same window.
Latest change = 7.0 − 10.0 = −3.0 mm  (down)  ✓
Range         = 10.0 − 4.0 = 6.0 mm             ✓
```

### Disagreement
```
IFS=7.0 mm, AIFS=3.0 mm → diff=+4.0 mm (IFS wetter)  ✓
```

## Tests

```bash
pytest -v                      # all tests
pytest tests/test_compute.py   # unit tests (PRD hand examples)
pytest tests/test_explain.py   # banned-word enforcement
pytest tests/test_api.py       # API schema + disclaimer
```

All tests run offline on fixture data. Never download in tests.

## Known limits

- 0.25° grid (~28 km). No local terrain or urban effects.
- ECMWF retains open data ~2–4 days. MonsoonDelta stores 14 days internally.
- AIFS is experimental; uncertainty properties differ from IFS.
- No ensemble probabilities.

## Deployment (Railway / Render / Fly.io)

1. Push to GitHub (this repo).
2. Connect repo to your host.
3. Set environment variables:
   - `STORE_DIR=/data/store`
   - `ECMWF_SOURCE=ecmwf`
   - `RETENTION_DAYS=14`
4. Mount persistent disk at `/data/store`.
5. Set ingest cron: `python -m ingest.run` every 3 hours.
6. Health check: `GET /api/health`.

See [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) for all design choices.

# MonsoonDelta 🌧️

**Bay of Bengal Precipitation Forecast Revision Platform**  
*Prepared for Durga Venkata Prasad Rapeti — QUEST Lab pre-doctoral Project 1*

[![MonsoonDelta CI](https://github.com/Rdvprasad36/Rain-Delta/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Rdvprasad36/Rain-Delta/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/Code%20License-MIT-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Data: CC BY 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Data%20License-CC%20BY%204.0-green.svg)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
[![Python 3.12+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12%2B-blue.svg)](https://python.org)

> ⚠️ **Mandatory Public Notice**:  
> *This is automated model output from ECMWF IFS and AIFS. It is not an official forecast or advisory. For official warnings and guidance, follow the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and local disaster management authorities.*

---

## 1. Overview & Core Features

MonsoonDelta tracks, revisions, and compares numerical weather prediction precipitation forecasts across cycles for the **Bay of Bengal** region (default focus: **Visakhapatnam ~17.7°N, 83.2°E**):

1. **Latest Forecast**: Synchronized 6-hour precipitation totals ($mm$) across the next 5 days for ECMWF's operational **IFS** (Integrated Forecasting System) and **AIFS** (AI-based Integrated Forecasting System).
2. **Forecast Revision Engine**: For any fixed 6-hour valid window, computes run-to-run drift across the last $N$ model cycles (latest change, full range, and direction trend: `up`, `down`, or `steady`).
3. **Model Disagreement**: Quantifies spatial and point-level delta ($D = \text{IFS} - \text{AIFS}$), pinpointing which model is wetter without deceptive relative percentages on trace amounts ($<1.0\,mm$).
4. **Deterministic Plain-Language Generator**: Rule-based template synthesizer that converts metrics into clear natural language, verified by CI against alarmist or unauthorized warning phrases.
5. **Interactive 3D Glassmorphic Interface**: High-performance UI featuring a real-time **Three.js** 3D globe and dynamic rainfall particle field, **Chart.js** forecast bar and revision trend lines, and a **Leaflet** divergence map.

---

## 2. System Architecture

### 2.1 Complete System Flow

```
                      ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │    ECMWF Open Data (data.ecmwf.int)    │
                      │  Public HTTPS • CC BY 4.0 • Zero Keys  │
                      └──────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                         │
                   Scheduled Ingest Job (Every 3 Hours)
                                         ▼
                 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │                ingest/run.py                   │
                 │  1. Check remote cycle against manifest.json   │
                 │  2. Download GRIB (IFS: 0p25, AIFS: 0p25)      │
                 │  3. GRIB Inspection: verify units key          │
                 │  4. Spatial Crop: 5–23°N, 78–100°E (Bay of B.) │
                 │  5. 14-Day Rolling History Retention Purge    │
                 └───────────────────────┬────────────────────────┘
                                         │
                              Writes compressed arrays
                                         ▼
                 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │       Persistent Store (/data/store)           │
                 │  ├── manifest.json                             │

### 2.2 Functional Layer Boundaries

|---|---|---|---|

| **Explain** | `src/monsoon/explain.py` | Deterministic template-based sentences | **Banned-word enforcement**: Rejects terms like `warning`, `alert`, `evacuate`. |
| **Constants** | `src/monsoon/constants.py` | Geobox bounds, tolerances, attribution | Single source of truth for calculations and legal texts. |
| **Ingest** | `ingest/run.py` | Downloads GRIBs, crops Bay of Bengal box, updates manifest | Scheduled asynchronously; never invoked during an API request. |
| **API** | `api/main.py` | FastAPI REST endpoints with caching and rate limits | Reads precomputed `.npy` store only. |

## 3. Mathematical Foundations & Hand Examples

All mathematical routines are derived from the project specification and verified against hand calculations in unit tests (`tests/test_compute.py`).

### 3.1 Unit Normalization
* **IFS**: Parameter `tp` (paramId `228`) is reported in **metres** ($m$).  
  $$\text{depth}\,(mm) = \text{value}\,(m) \times 1000$$
* **AIFS**: Parameter `tp` (paramId `228228`) is reported in **$\text{kg m}^{-2}$**.  
  $$\text{depth}\,(mm) = \text{value}\,(\text{kg m}^{-2}) \times 1.0 \quad (\text{for liquid water at } 1000\,\text{kg/m}^3)$$
* **Guard rule**: Any unexpected unit string triggers an immediate `ValueError`.

### 3.2 6-Hour Window Accumulation
Total precipitation is cumulative from forecast inception ($t=0$):
$$W(s) = tp(s) - tp(s - 6) \quad \text{with} \quad tp(0) = 0$$

*Hand-Checked Example*:
- IFS: $tp(12h) = 0.002\,m$, $tp(18h) = 0.005\,m$ $\implies W(18h) = 5.0 - 2.0 = \mathbf{3.0\,mm}$
- AIFS: $tp(12h) = 2.0\,\text{kg/m}^2$, $tp(18h) = 5.0\,\text{kg/m}^2$ $\implies W(18h) = 5.0 - 2.0 = \mathbf{3.0\,mm}$

### 3.3 Forecast Revision
For valid time window $V$, across runs $r_1, r_2, \dots, r_k$:
- $\text{Latest Change} = A_{\text{latest}} - A_{\text{previous}}$
- $\text{Range} = \max(A_r) - \min(A_r)$
- $\text{Direction} = \begin{cases} \text{steady} & \text{if } |\text{Latest Change}| < 0.5\,mm \\ \text{up} & \text{if } \text{Latest Change} \ge +0.5\,mm \\ \text{down} & \text{if } \text{Latest Change} \le -0.5\,mm \end{cases}$

*Hand-Checked Example*:  
Runs $00Z \to 06Z \to 12Z$ yield $4.0\,mm, 10.0\,mm, 7.0\,mm$:
$$\text{Latest Change} = 7.0 - 10.0 = \mathbf{-3.0\,mm\,(down)}, \quad \text{Range} = 10.0 - 4.0 = \mathbf{6.0\,mm}$$

### 3.4 Disagreement
$$D = \text{IFS} - \text{AIFS}$$
Relative percentage difference is withheld when both $\text{IFS} < 1.0\,mm$ and $\text{AIFS} < 1.0\,mm$ to prevent misleading ratios on trace amounts.

## 4. Complete Deployment Guidelines

MonsoonDelta is designed for high reliability, minimal resource footprint, and zero operational cost. Below are step-by-step instructions for popular hosting environments.

  "attribution": "This service is based on data and products of ECMWF...",

set -e

# Run background ingest worker loop if enabled
if [ "${ENABLE_INGEST_WORKER:-true}" = "true" ]; then
  echo "[MonsoonDelta] Spawning background ingest worker (every 3 hours)..."
  (
    while true; do
      echo "[MonsoonDelta Ingest] Checking ECMWF open data at $(date -u)..."
      python -m ingest.run || echo "[MonsoonDelta Ingest] Cycle check finished."
      sleep 10800
    done

FROM python:3.12-slim

LABEL maintainer="Durga Venkata Prasad Rapeti <rdvprasad36@gmail.com>"
LABEL description="MonsoonDelta — ECMWF IFS/AIFS precipitation forecast revision app"

    libeccodes-dev \
    libeccodes-tools \
    wget \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Install Python dependencies
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy application code
COPY src/     src/
COPY api/     api/
COPY ingest/  ingest/
COPY frontend/ frontend/
COPY scripts/ scripts/

RUN chmod +x /app/scripts/start.sh

# Create store directory

ENV STORE_DIR=/data/store
ENV PYTHONPATH=/app/src:/app

EXPOSE 8000

# Start via start.sh (auto-binds to $PORT and spawns background ingest worker)

services:
  api:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    volumes:

      - STORE_DIR=/data/store

      interval: 60s
      timeout: 10s

      start_period: 20s

    volumes:

    environment:
